newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai sees boom in executive head-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai sees boom in executive head-hunting.

text.p: Management head-hunting firms in Shanghai are growing very fast due to a shortage of skilled managers and growing competition for staff among foreign companies, the Business News and analysts said on Monday.

The search for trained executives has become so competitive that foreign companies are banding together and establishing "non-poaching" deals amongst each other to prevent their staff leaving for other firms, an industry analyst said.
The Business News said Shanghai's largest management search company, Chengda Senior Executive Consultancy, tripled its business in 1996, and other companies also grew fast.
"You've got competitors in many ways agreeing not to steal each other's people," the industry analyst said.

The newspaper said that Shanghai currently has around 100 headhunting companies, including some start-up firms that it described as "carpetbaggers who specialize in shady business," attracted to the business by its explosive growth.
